evidence.text:
劉尹王長史同坐長史酒酣起舞劉尹曰阿奴今日
不復減向子期

judgment.explanation: 嵇康 is the canonical full name of Ji Kang, who is the person being visited by Zhong Hui in this passage. The main text explicitly names 嵇康 as the person whom 鍾士季 goes to seek. The candidate matches the historical Ji Kang.

鍾㑹 (鍾會) is the full name of Zhong Hui, the person who went to visit Ji Kang. The Liu annotation explicitly states '魏氏春秋曰鍾㑹為大將軍兄弟所暱聞康名' identifying 鍾㑹 as the visitor. The candidate 鍾士季 is the same person (Zhong Hui, courtesy name Shiji).

鍾士季 is the surname plus courtesy name of Zhong Hui, the main figure in this passage who goes to visit Ji Kang. The main text opens with '鍾士季精有才理先不識嵇康' establishing him as the protagonist. The candidate 鍾士季 is the same historical person as Zhong Hui.

The surface 康 in the Liu annotation refers to Ji Kang (嵇康). The main text explicitly names 嵇康, and the annotation '聞康名' refers to Zhong Hui hearing of Ji Kang's name, consistent with the main narrative about Zhong Hui visiting Ji Kang.

The surface 康 in the annotation '譛康焉' refers to Ji Kang, the object of Zhong Hui's slander. The main text establishes Ji Kang as the person Zhong Hui visited, and the annotation continues this narrative about the slander against Ji Kang.

The surface 康 in the Liu annotation refers to Ji Kang, described as skilled at forging iron (能鍜鐵). The main text describes Ji Kang forging under a tree, and the annotation elaborates on this same person's skill at iron forging.

review.explanation: The surface 嵇康 appears verbatim in the main text as the person Zhong Hui seeks out. The canonical name match is exact, and the historical referent (Ji Kang, the famous Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove figure) is unambiguous. The main text explicitly names 嵇康 as the person being visited, and the surrounding narrative about forging iron and the encounter with Zhong Hui is consistent with the historical Ji Kang. No contradicting evidence exists.

The surface 向子期 is the courtesy name of 向秀 (Xiang Xiu), one of the Seven Sages of the Bamboo Grove. The main text explicitly places 向子期 as 嵇康's assistant at the forge (向子期為佐鼔排), which matches the historical relationship between Xiang Xiu and Ji Kang. The alias registry evidence confirms 向子期 as a known alias for 向秀. The historical referent is unambiguous given the context of Ji Kang forging iron with Xiang Xiu assisting.

The surface 康 in the Liu annotation '聞康名' refers to Ji Kang. The annotation is about Zhong Hui hearing of Kang's name, which directly continues the main text narrative about Zhong Hui seeking out Ji Kang. The coreference with other Ji Kang mentions in the story is well-supported. The annotation context (鍾㑹為大將軍兄弟所暱聞康名) is consistent with the historical account of Zhong Hui's interest in Ji Kang.

The surface 康 in the annotation '譛康焉' refers to Ji Kang as the object of Zhong Hui's slander. This directly continues the narrative arc from the main text where Zhong Hui visits Ji Kang and the annotations describe Zhong Hui's resentment (㑹深衘之). The slander of Ji Kang by Zhong Hui is a well-documented historical event. The coreference chain linking this mention to other Ji Kang mentions in the story is consistent and supported by the narrative flow.

The mention surface '康' appears in the Liu annotation (sfh1-ev-24-jianao-003-liu-annotation-002) which discusses 康 (Ji Kang) forging iron under a willow tree. The main text (sfh1-ev-24-jianao-003-main) explicitly names 嵇康 and describes the same forging scene with 向子期 assisting. The annotation's reference to 康 forging iron directly parallels the main text's description of 嵇康 forging, confirming the anaphoric reference. The candidate evidence (sfh1-candidate-evidence-da16863f7be828a23ec7) provides the canonical name 嵇康. The annotation text '康性絶巧能鍜鐵家有盛栁樹' matches the main text's '康方大樹下鍜' scene, providing strong contextual and semantic support for identity. No contradicting evidence exists.
